basis: CEL-MODY combines endocrine pancreatic failure causing diabetes with characteristic exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.
Ichthyosis, congenital oral abnormalities and digital malformations jointly define this syndrome.
Inherited loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue defines this metabolic disorder; hepatic and other complications vary across subtypes.
Ichthyosis defines the disorder; intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 30-79%. Typical X-linked ichthyosis corneal deposits do not impair vision.
Congenital pericardial cyst; pulmonary symptoms do not establish lung damage, and serious complications are rare.
Inherited tubulointerstitial kidney disease causes progressive renal dysfunction; hyperuricemia is variable and does not define a separate metabolic disorder.
Hereditary meningioma arises in the meninges of the central nervous system.
Chondrodysplasia and gonadal endocrine failure define it; CNS anomalies/ID occur in 75-99%, iris/optic coloboma in 2/2. Nail dysplasia 1/2 omitted at cap.
Cerebral vascular malformations define the disease; brain hemorrhage occurs in 15/28 and seizures in 10/28.
Complex I metabolic defect; gliosis and dystonia in 1/1 support CNS damage. Apnea can be central; cardiomyopathy frequency is unspecified.
Familial excess of red blood cells; thrombosis is a variable complication rather than a defining vascular lesion.
Congenital distal joint contractures: camptodactyly in 12/12 and restricted forearm rotation in 7/11.
Skin/nail abnormalities, marrow failure and oral leukoplakia define dyskeratosis congenita. Pulmonary fibrosis 3/12 is below 30%; liver disease is less frequent.
Complex I defect; neurologic disease 3/3, rod-cone dystrophy 1/3 and progressive sensorineural hearing loss 1/3. Muscle weakness lacks evidence of primary myopathy.
Inherited dental enamel hypomaturation and hypomineralization; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Amoebic infection directly inflames and destroys brain tissue; additional disseminated sites are not consistently involved.
Primary skeletal muscle disease with tubular inclusions, myopathic changes and progressive weakness.
Benign smooth muscle neoplasms confined to the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Benign neoplasm originates in the gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Atrial electrical rhythm disorder of the heart.
B-lymphoblast malignancy of blood/marrow and lymphoid tissue; the leukemia/lymphoma entity also warrants the lymphoma mechanism axis.
Demyelinating/axonal peripheral neuropathy; persistent skeletal deformities include pes cavus 5/5 and hammertoes 3/5, with distal muscle atrophy 6/6.
Spastic paraplegia with kyphosis 9/9 and pectus carinatum 7/9. Hypertrichosis is cosmetic; hearing impairment is below 30%.
Congenital eyelid malformations define BPES; ovarian endocrine failure characterizes type I, with amenorrhea reported in 2/3 females; type II lacks ovarian failure.
Mitochondrial myopathy with weakness and elevated CK in 4/4; learning disability in 4/4 supports neurologic involvement. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness.
